title: Healey and Minogue Clash in Final Massachusetts Gubernatorial Debate
text:
In the final debate before Election Day, Democratic Governor Maura Healey and Republican challenger Mike Minogue engaged in a contentious exchange focusing on affordability, President Trump, and abortion access. Healey criticized Trump's economic policies for driving inflation and accused Minogue of not trusting women, while Minogue defended his pro-life stance based on faith and pledged to uphold the law.
Gov. Maura Healey and Republican challenger Mike Minogue participate in the final gubernatorial debate at WCVB on Oct. 15, 2026 in Needham. Gov.
Maura Healey and challenger Mike Minogue shared a stage but little else Thursday, as the Democrat and Republican savaged each other's positions during their last debate before Election Day. Their disputes centered around two hallmark themes: affordability and President Trump. Both issues have come to define this election and dozens of others across the country.
But the overall testiness of the evening flared across a number of topics, including abortion and the situation around a Healey administration worker who was arrested and charged with distributing cocaine.
"I will follow the law. I believe in the separation of church and state and when I become governor, I will swear an oath to do that," Minogue said.
"Now I am still allowed to have my own beliefs, but my own beliefs will not get in the way of me doing what I'm supposed to do in upholding the law. " "It's not politicizing something when one in three women in America live without access to needed abortion care," Healey said. "I trust women. I trust women and their doctors.
Mike Minogue doesn't. Mike Minogue doesn't," she said, repeating the last sentence. Minogue responded by accusing Healey of"attacking our faith," and cited his wife, daughter and former colleagues as women he holds in high regard. Minogue has described himself as pro-life, rooted in his Catholic faith.
Affordability dominated the conversation across several issues including transit, energy affordability, and housing, with Healey continually blasting President Trump's policies and actions and blaming them for inflation and costs spiraling out of control for most people.
"We're only having this conversation because we have a president who's taken us to war, who long ago put on tariffs, and has done other things that have raised the cost of everything," Healey said. In all, she invoked Trump 13 times Thursday, piling on to the more than 30 presidential citations she made in a previous debate with Minogue. Minogue redirected to Healey's time in office and state policies he said were spiking bills for state residents.
First up: Cutting the state's tax on gasoline.
"We need to cut the gas tax now. Yes, it went up because of the Iran war, but we can give people immediate relief," Minogue said. Republican challenger Mike Minogue participates in the final gubernatorial debate with Gov. Maura Healey at WCVB on Oct. 15, 2026 in Needham.
On housing, Minogue pushed back on Healey's claim that she has worked to help people build homes"as quickly as possible.
"Minogue said whatever progress Massachusetts has made was thanks to her Republican predecessor. "We have built homes, but the things that are being built are all based on Charlie Baker's term. Gov. Healey is last in the nation for permits per person," Minogue said.
Instead, he said, the state should reduce the time to get home-building permits to 45 days to help speed up the construction, and said he would work with cities and towns to ease so-called"stretch" building codes, which include higher standards for cities and towns that have opted for Green Community designation.
"Healey shot back that the state has already cut back the amount of time it takes to get state permits to 30 days. On energy bills, Minogue launched a salvo attacking Healey for blocking natural gas pipeline expansion. Healey pushed back, saying she stopped a developer from sticking taxpayers with the bill for building a new line, and that she's asked for federal help in expanding existing lines.
She said she’s also focused on expanding the energy menu, supporting solar, wind, geothermal and hydroelectric projects.
"But right now? People's energy bills, people's energy costs, they're being driven up by a war we shouldn't be in and tariffs, all the result of Donald Trump, a man that my opponent supported," said Healey, referring to Minogue.
"There's no war in Connecticut and Pennsylvania. You know what's in Pennsylvania? Massive natural resources of natural gas that we need to bring in that Attorney General Maura Healey stopped," Minogue said. The candidates again sniped at each other while discussing the years of scandal plaguing the state police, including a recent report of a sexual assault inside the state police barracks on Martha's Vineyard.
A school security administrator visiting a trooper was allowed to enter the facility where he reportedly assaulted a woman he’d met at a bar, according to a"It starts with the leader, and we have to make sure we have high expectations," Minogue said. Healey lauded the leadership of State Police Col. Jeffrey Noble, whom she hired from outside the ranks to lead the "Do things happen? Sometimes things happen.
But I can tell you, he and I make sure swift action is taken," she said.
"I think the governor just said 'sometimes things happen. ' That is unacceptable. A woman was raped," Minogue said. Minogue said the case is one of several examples of what he called Healey's lack of leadership.
He cited athe state made to a former MBTA worker after T head and interim state transportation secretary Phil Eng reportedly pulled her hair at a work event. Gov. Maura Healey participates in the final gubernatorial debate against Republican challenger Mike Minogue at WCVB on Oct. 15, 2026 in Needham. But the pair would return more than once to the case of LaMar Cook.
The Healey administration employee was arrested earlier this year after investigators accused him of having eight kilograms of cocaine delivered to his state office. Cook was fired following that arrest. He made headlines again this week, when the U.S. Attorney for Massachusetts Leah Foley filed federal fraud charges against him, saying Cook fraudulently signed up for SNAP benefits.
“ Someone can get 18 pounds of cocaine delivered, and you didn't fire them, they got arrested," Minogue said to Healey. "Then they got severance. And now they're on SNAP benefits that you didn't even check on.
" He also called for a full investigation into where the cocaine was headed and how it hadn’t been caught sooner. "I did fire LaMar Cook immediately, and I will fire anyone immediately who commits wrongdoing in my administration," Healey said. " If someone is arrested, you didn't fire them. They got arrested with 18 pounds of cocaine," he said.
"In the real world, you're automatically fired. " Turning to the Immigration and Customs Enforcement's crackdown on undocumented immigrants, Minogue said he would work with ICE to take criminals off the streets and reduce the public safety threat, rather than antagonize the federal agency and agents. Healey, meanwhile, pointed to the federal immigration enforcement in the state as the reason things feel so hot.
"People are afraid to go to school because of ICE," she said, later adding,"The problem is ICE. ICE is the public safety threat.
" Paul Wantanabe, a political science professor at UMass Boston, said overall Healey emerged largely how she fared going into Thursday night’s debate and was able to parry Minogue’s attacks on her leadership. And while Minogue"proved to be more than just his ads,” Watanabe said Minogue failed to lay out the big agenda underlying his case to be governor. Nonetheless, Watanabe thought the tenor of the debate and the clash of ideas was substantive in an era of hyperpartisanship.
“ It was not a battle between somebody who was a MAGA convert in a big way, and somebody who was a die-hard Massachusetts liberal,” Watanabe said. Thursday was the last face-to-face meeting scheduled between the candidates before Election Day, coming just as Massachusetts voters gear up to make their choices. More than 600,000 mail-in ballots were sent to residents last week, with another 300,000 awaiting delivery, according to Secretary of the Commonwealth's Bill Galvin's office.
And in-person early voting begins on Saturday. The debate was hosted by WBUR, WCVB Channel 5, the Boston Globe, El Planeta and the Bay State Banner. Massachusetts has a penchant for bucking its deep-blue reputation when picking governors, having elected several Republicans to the job through the years. But Minogue has some work to do if he wants to join their ranks..
Healey led both polls with more than 50% of the total vote, while Minogue garnered less than 40% of support from respondents. In first Healey-Minogue debate, lots of talk of affordability, the governor's record and Trump's impact
